page: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 32 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6448H processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system features an x86_64 architecture with a shared CPU allocation and no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 375.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.72 GB per core. For acceleration, the server bundles two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 2200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance across multiple domains, particularly in GPU-accelerated tasks. LLM inference speeds for a medium 7B model reach 6275.36 tokens per second for prompt processing and 141.42 tokens per second for text generation, placing it in the top tier. CPU performance is also robust, with a Passmark CPU score of 64768.69 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 62892.75. Memory bandwidth is strong for read operations, reaching 4985.78 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 211.9 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though write bandwidth is average at 88.2 GB/sec.

The server offers high resource density, combining substantial GPU memory with a large system memory footprint, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient platform for medium-scale AI workloads. However, the shared CPU allocation and a relatively modest 2.0 GHz base clock speed represent a tradeoff for workloads requiring dedicated, high-frequency single-core CPU performance. This server is highly suited for LLM inference, machine learning model training, data science pipelines, and database operations that benefit from GPU acceleration and fast local NVMe storage.
description: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a GPU-accelerated cloud server designed for demanding computational workloads. It features 32 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6448H processor at 2.0 GHz, paired with 375.0 GB of system memory and a 2200 GB NVMe SSD. The server's primary acceleration comes from two NVIDIA L40S GPUs with Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a total of 96 GB of VRAM. Benchmarks show top-tier performance in LLM inference, with a medium 7B model achieving 6275.36 tokens per second for prompt processing. While the shared CPU allocation and 2.0 GHz clock speed present a tradeoff for single-core CPU-bound tasks, the server's massive GPU and system memory capacity make it highly cost-efficient for resource-intensive workloads. It is best suited for machine learning inference, data science pipelines, and database operations.
